/-!
# Conjecture 2.82

by A. I. Shirshov

Can the class of groups with the $n$th Engel condition
$[x, \underbrace{y, \ldots, y}_{n}] = 1$ be defined by identical relations of the form
$u = v$, where $u$ and $v$ are words without negative powers of variables? This can be done
for $n = 1, 2, 3$ (A. I. Shirshov, *Algebra i Logika* **2**, no. 5 (1963), 5–18).

Editors' comment: this has also been done for $n = 4$ (G. Traustason, *J. Group Theory* **2**,
no. 1 (1999), 39–46). As remarked by O. Macedońska, this is also true for the class of locally
graded $n$-Engel groups, because such a group is locally nilpotent (Y. Kim, A. Rhemtulla,
*Groups–Korea '94*, de Gruyter, 1995, 189–197) and then an extension of a nilpotent group of
$n$-bounded class by a group of $n$-bounded exponent (R. G. Burns, Yu. Medvedev,
*J. Austral. Math. Soc.* **64** (1998), 92–100); a classical result of Mal'cev then implies that
such groups satisfy a positive law.

A *positive word* is an element of the free monoid on countably many variables
$x_0, x_1, \ldots$ (the empty word is allowed). A group $G$ *satisfies the positive law* $u = v$
if $u$ and $v$ take the same value under every assignment of elements of $G$ to the variables.
"The class of $n$-Engel groups can be defined by identical relations of the form $u = v$"
means that there is a set $S$ of positive laws such that a group is $n$-Engel if and only if it
satisfies every law in $S$. Commutators are taken in the notebook's convention
$[a, b] = a^{-1} b^{-1} a b$, and $[x, y, \ldots, y]$ is left-normed.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
def engelCommutator (x y : G) : ℕ → G
  | 0 => x
  | n + 1 => (engelCommutator x y n)⁻¹ * y⁻¹ * engelCommutator x y n * y
blocks.docstring:
The left-normed iterated commutator $[x,\, {}_n y] = [x, \underbrace{y, \ldots, y}_{n}]$,
defined by $[x,\, {}_0 y] = x$ and $[x,\, {}_{n+1} y] = [[x,\, {}_n y], y]$, where
$[a, b] = a^{-1} b^{-1} a b$ is the commutator in the convention of the Kourovka Notebook.
Mathlib's `⁅a, b⁆` is `a * b * a⁻¹ * b⁻¹`; for a fixed $n$ the two conventions are not
known to give the same class of $n$-Engel groups, so the notebook's convention is spelled
out.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Kourovka.«1.40».engelCommutator (uses Mathlib's ⁅a,b⁆ = a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹; lives in another problem file and Kourovka files do not cross-import); Mathlib's commutatorElement.
justification.name: Kourovka.«2.82».engelCommutator
justification.why_needed: Left-normed iterated commutator [x, y, …, y] with n copies of y; no such definition in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib. Defined with the notebook's convention [a,b] = a⁻¹b⁻¹ab (see modeling decisions).

blocks.name: engelCommutator
blocks.text:
/-- The left-normed iterated commutator $[x,\, {}_n y] = [x, \underbrace{y, \ldots, y}_{n}]$,
defined by $[x,\, {}_0 y] = x$ and $[x,\, {}_{n+1} y] = [[x,\, {}_n y], y]$, where
$[a, b] = a^{-1} b^{-1} a b$ is the commutator in the convention of the Kourovka Notebook.
Mathlib's `⁅a, b⁆` is `a * b * a⁻¹ * b⁻¹`; for a fixed $n$ the two conventions are not
known to give the same class of $n$-Engel groups, so the notebook's convention is spelled
out. -/
def engelCommutator (x y : G) : ℕ → G
  | 0 => x
  | n + 1 => (engelCommutator x y n)⁻¹ * y⁻¹ * engelCommutator x y n * y

blocks.code:
def IsNEngelGroup (n : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : G, engelCommutator x y n = 1
blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ satisfies the $n$th Engel condition (is an $n$-Engel group) if
$[x, \underbrace{y, \ldots, y}_{n}] = 1$ for all $x, y \in G$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: LieAlgebra.IsEngelian / Kourovka.«1.40».IsEngelGroup (the latter is the unbounded Engel condition ∃ n, not a fixed n).
justification.name: Kourovka.«2.82».IsNEngelGroup
justification.why_needed: The n-th Engel condition ∀ x y, [x, y, …, y] = 1 (n copies of y). Mathlib has Engel notions only for Lie algebras (Mathlib.Algebra.Lie.Engel), not for groups.

blocks.name: IsNEngelGroup
blocks.text:
/-- A group $G$ satisfies the $n$th Engel condition (is an $n$-Engel group) if
$[x, \underbrace{y, \ldots, y}_{n}] = 1$ for all $x, y \in G$. -/
def IsNEngelGroup (n : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : G, engelCommutator x y n = 1

blocks.code:
def SatisfiesPositiveLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] (u v : FreeMonoid ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeMonoid.lift f u = FreeMonoid.lift f v
blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ satisfies the positive law $u = v$, where $u$ and $v$ are positive words in the
variables $x_0, x_1, \ldots$ (elements of `FreeMonoid ℕ`), if $u$ and $v$ take the same value in
$G$ under every assignment of elements of $G$ to the variables.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FreeMonoid.lift (used inside the definition); FreeGroup.lift (inappropriate since it would allow negative powers).
justification.name: Kourovka.«2.82».SatisfiesPositiveLaw
justification.why_needed: A group satisfies the identical relation u = v for positive words u v : FreeMonoid ℕ if FreeMonoid.lift f u = FreeMonoid.lift f v for all f : ℕ → G. Mathlib has no notion of a group satisfying a (positive) law / variety of groups.

blocks.name: SatisfiesPositiveLaw
blocks.text:
/-- A group $G$ satisfies the positive law $u = v$, where $u$ and $v$ are positive words in the
variables $x_0, x_1, \ldots$ (elements of `FreeMonoid ℕ`), if $u$ and $v$ take the same value in
$G$ under every assignment of elements of $G$ to the variables. -/
def SatisfiesPositiveLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] (u v : FreeMonoid ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeMonoid.lift f u = FreeMonoid.lift f v

blocks.code:
def IsLocallyGraded (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → H ≠ ⊥ → ∃ K : Subgroup H, K ≠ ⊤ ∧ K.FiniteIndex
blocks.docstring:
A group is *locally graded* if every non-trivial finitely generated subgroup has a proper
subgroup of finite index (equivalently, a non-trivial finite quotient).

justification.closest_existing_considered: Subgroup.FG, Subgroup.FiniteIndex (used as building blocks); no residual-finiteness or local-gradedness predicate exists in Mathlib.
justification.name: Kourovka.«2.82».IsLocallyGraded
justification.why_needed: Locally graded groups (every non-trivial finitely generated subgroup has a proper subgroup of finite index) are not in Mathlib or the repo.

blocks.name: IsLocallyGraded
blocks.text:
/-- A group is *locally graded* if every non-trivial finitely generated subgroup has a proper
subgroup of finite index (equivalently, a non-trivial finite quotient). -/
def IsLocallyGraded (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → H ≠ ⊥ → ∃ K : Subgroup H, K ≠ ⊤ ∧ K.FiniteIndex

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isNEngelGroup_one_iff : IsNEngelGroup 1 G ↔ ∀ x y : G, x * y = y * x := by
  simp only [IsNEngelGroup, engelCommutator_one, commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm]
  exact ⟨fun h x y ↦ by simpa using h x⁻¹ y⁻¹, fun h x y ↦ h x⁻¹ y⁻¹⟩
blocks.docstring: The $1$-Engel groups are exactly the abelian groups.
blocks.name: isNEngelGroup_one_iff
blocks.text:

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isNEngelGroup_one_iff : IsNEngelGroup 1 G ↔ ∀ x y : G, x * y = y * x := by
  simp only [IsNEngelGroup, engelCommutator_one, commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm]
  exact ⟨fun h x y ↦ by simpa using h x⁻¹ y⁻¹, fun h x y ↦ h x⁻¹ y⁻¹⟩

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem satisfiesPositiveLaw_of_mul_of_iff :
    SatisfiesPositiveLaw G (.of 0 * .of 1) (.of 1 * .of 0) ↔ ∀ x y : G, x * y = y * x := by
  refine ⟨fun h x y ↦ ?_, fun h f ↦ by simp [h]⟩
  simpa using h (fun i ↦ if i = 0 then x else y)
blocks.docstring: The positive law $x_0 x_1 = x_1 x_0$ holds in $G$ exactly when $G$ is abelian.

blocks.text:

  refine ⟨fun h x y ↦ ?_, fun h f ↦ by simp [h]⟩
  simpa using h (fun i ↦ if i = 0 then x else y)

blocks.docstring:
Within the class of locally graded groups, the $n$-Engel groups can be defined by identical
relations of the form $u = v$, where $u$ and $v$ are words without negative powers of variables:
for every $n \ge 1$ there is a set $S$ of positive laws such that a locally graded group $G$ is
$n$-Engel if and only if $G$ satisfies every law in $S$ (remark of O. Macedońska).

The editors' justification is that a locally graded $n$-Engel group is locally nilpotent
(Kim–Rhemtulla), hence an extension of a nilpotent group of $n$-bounded class by a group of
$n$-bounded exponent (Burns–Medvedev), and hence satisfies a positive law (Mal'cev).

claims.decomposer_note: Implicit universal quantifier over n (intended n ≥ 1; n = 0 gives the trivial variety, harmlessly definable by x = y); the Prop is: for every n there exists a (possibly infinite) set S of pairs of positive words (elements of a free monoid on countably many variables, empty word allowed; nonemptiness is immaterial since ℤ ∈ 𝓔_n) such that for every group G, G satisfies the left-normed n-Engel law [x,y,…,y]=1 (n copies of y, defined as in Kourovka/1_40.lean's engelCommutator) iff every law u=v in S holds under all assignments of variables in G; the biconditional over all groups constrains S (S = ∅ would make every group n-Engel), so answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n, ∃ S, ∀ G, … is non-vacuous; quantify G over `Type` as in the other Kourovka files.
claims.reviewer_why: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n ≥ 1, ∃ S : Set (FreeMonoid ℕ × FreeMonoid ℕ), ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsNEngelGroup n G ↔ ∀ w ∈ S, SatisfiesPositiveLaw G w.1 w.2. Same logical shape as all other candidates (positive words = FreeMonoid ℕ, empty word allowed, S possibly infinite, biconditional over all groups so S = ∅ is ruled out), but c01 is the only candidate that defines the iterated commutator in the notebook's convention [a,b] = a⁻¹b⁻¹ab. Under Mathlib's ⁅a,b⁆ = aba⁻¹b⁻¹ (c02–c08) the n-Engel class provably agrees only for n ≤ 3; for n = 4 it is equivalent (within 4-Engel groups) to the extra law [[x,y,y],[x,y,y,y]] = 1 and for general n no equivalence is known, so those candidates risk stating a different class. Minor docstring edits only.

decomposition_objections.text: 1. The note '(defined as in Kourovka/1_40.lean's engelCommutator)' would tie the n-Engel condition to Mathlib's ⁅a,b⁆ = a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹, whereas the notebook uses [a,b] = a⁻¹b⁻¹ab. For fixed n the two conventions are provably equivalent for n ≤ 3 but not obviously for n ≥ 4, so following the hint literally risks stating a subtly different class of groups; I kept the left-normed shape and n copies of y but used the notebook's convention. 2. For the locally graded slot, the editors' sketch (Kim–Rhemtulla, Burns–Medvedev, Mal'cev) literally justifies only that locally graded n-Engel groups satisfy some non-trivial positive law; the 'defined for the class' reading, which the table prescribes and I stated as research solved, additionally needs that a locally graded group satisfying all positive laws of the locally graded n-Engel groups is n-Engel (this does follow from Burns–Macedońska–Medvedev's theorem that locally graded groups satisfying a positive law are nilpotent-by-finite-exponent together with the fact that relatively free groups of a variety satisfying a positive law are groups of fractions of their positive subsemigroups, but the notebook does not spell this out). 3. Minor: the note that Traustason's 1999 result 'depends on the local nilpotence of 4-Engel groups (Havas–Vaughan-Lee)' is chronologically off (Havas–Vaughan-Lee is from 2005); this does not affect the formal statement.

# Conjecture 2.82

by A. I. Shirshov

Can the class of groups with the $n$th Engel condition
$[x, \underbrace{y, \ldots, y}_{n}] = 1$ be defined by identical relations of the form
$u = v$, where $u$ and $v$ are words without negative powers of variables? This can be done
for $n = 1, 2, 3$ (A. I. Shirshov, *Algebra i Logika* **2**, no. 5 (1963), 5–18).

Editors' comment: this has also been done for $n = 4$ (G. Traustason, *J. Group Theory* **2**,
no. 1 (1999), 39–46). As remarked by O. Macedońska, this is also true for the class of locally
graded $n$-Engel groups, because such a group is locally nilpotent (Y. Kim, A. Rhemtulla,
*Groups–Korea '94*, de Gruyter, 1995, 189–197) and then an extension of a nilpotent group of
$n$-bounded class by a group of $n$-bounded exponent (R. G. Burns, Yu. Medvedev,
*J. Austral. Math. Soc.* **64** (1998), 92–100); a classical result of Mal'cev then implies that
such groups satisfy a positive law.

A *positive word* is an element of the free monoid on countably many variables
$x_0, x_1, \ldots$ (the empty word is allowed). A group $G$ *satisfies the positive law* $u = v$
if $u$ and $v$ take the same value under every assignment of elements of $G$ to the variables.
"The class of $n$-Engel groups can be defined by identical relations of the form $u = v$"
means that there is a set $S$ of positive laws such that a group is $n$-Engel if and only if it
satisfies every law in $S$. Commutators are taken in the notebook's convention
$[a, b] = a^{-1} b^{-1} a b$, and $[x, y, \ldots, y]$ is left-normed.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«2.82»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- The left-normed iterated commutator $[x,\, {}_n y] = [x, \underbrace{y, \ldots, y}_{n}]$,
defined by $[x,\, {}_0 y] = x$ and $[x,\, {}_{n+1} y] = [[x,\, {}_n y], y]$, where
$[a, b] = a^{-1} b^{-1} a b$ is the commutator in the convention of the Kourovka Notebook.
Mathlib's `⁅a, b⁆` is `a * b * a⁻¹ * b⁻¹`; for a fixed $n$ the two conventions are not
known to give the same class of $n$-Engel groups, so the notebook's convention is spelled
out. -/
def engelCommutator (x y : G) : ℕ → G
  | 0 => x
  | n + 1 => (engelCommutator x y n)⁻¹ * y⁻¹ * engelCommutator x y n * y

/-- A group $G$ satisfies the $n$th Engel condition (is an $n$-Engel group) if
$[x, \underbrace{y, \ldots, y}_{n}] = 1$ for all $x, y \in G$. -/
def IsNEngelGroup (n : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : G, engelCommutator x y n = 1

/-- A group $G$ satisfies the positive law $u = v$, where $u$ and $v$ are positive words in the
variables $x_0, x_1, \ldots$ (elements of `FreeMonoid ℕ`), if $u$ and $v$ take the same value in
$G$ under every assignment of elements of $G$ to the variables. -/
def SatisfiesPositiveLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] (u v : FreeMonoid ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeMonoid.lift f u = FreeMonoid.lift f v

/-- A group is *locally graded* if every non-trivial finitely generated subgroup has a proper
subgroup of finite index (equivalently, a non-trivial finite quotient). -/
def IsLocallyGraded (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → H ≠ ⊥ → ∃ K : Subgroup H, K ≠ ⊤ ∧ K.FiniteIndex

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem engelCommutator_one (x y : G) : engelCommutator x y 1 = ⁅x⁻¹, y⁻¹⁆ := by
  simp [engelCommutator, commutatorElement_def]

/-- The $1$-Engel groups are exactly the abelian groups. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isNEngelGroup_one_iff : IsNEngelGroup 1 G ↔ ∀ x y : G, x * y = y * x := by
  simp only [IsNEngelGroup, engelCommutator_one, commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm]
  exact ⟨fun h x y ↦ by simpa using h x⁻¹ y⁻¹, fun h x y ↦ h x⁻¹ y⁻¹⟩

/-- The positive law $x_0 x_1 = x_1 x_0$ holds in $G$ exactly when $G$ is abelian. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem satisfiesPositiveLaw_of_mul_of_iff :
    SatisfiesPositiveLaw G (.of 0 * .of 1) (.of 1 * .of 0) ↔ ∀ x y : G, x * y = y * x := by
  refine ⟨fun h x y ↦ ?_, fun h f ↦ by simp [h]⟩
  simpa using h (fun i ↦ if i = 0 then x else y)

/--
Can the class of groups with the $n$th Engel condition $[x, \underbrace{y, \ldots, y}_{n}] = 1$
be defined by identical relations of the form $u = v$, where $u$ and $v$ are words without
negative powers of variables?

That is: for every $n \ge 1$, is there a set $S$ of positive laws such that a group $G$ is
$n$-Engel if and only if $G$ satisfies every law $u = v$ in $S$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.82» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → ∃ S : Set (FreeMonoid ℕ × FreeMonoid ℕ),
      ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
        IsNEngelGroup n G ↔ ∀ w ∈ S, SatisfiesPositiveLaw G w.1 w.2 := by
  sorry

/--
For $n = 1, 2, 3$ the class of $n$-Engel groups can be defined by identical relations of the
form $u = v$, where $u$ and $v$ are words without negative powers of variables
(A. I. Shirshov, *Algebra i Logika* **2**, no. 5 (1963), 5–18).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.82».variants.n_le_three (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (hn' : n ≤ 3) :
    ∃ S : Set (FreeMonoid ℕ × FreeMonoid ℕ),
      ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
        IsNEngelGroup n G ↔ ∀ w ∈ S, SatisfiesPositiveLaw G w.1 w.2 := by
  sorry

/--
The class of $4$-Engel groups can be defined by identical relations of the form $u = v$, where
$u$ and $v$ are words without negative powers of variables
(G. Traustason, *J. Group Theory* **2**, no. 1 (1999), 39–46).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.82».variants.n_eq_four :
    ∃ S : Set (FreeMonoid ℕ × FreeMonoid ℕ),
      ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
        IsNEngelGroup 4 G ↔ ∀ w ∈ S, SatisfiesPositiveLaw G w.1 w.2 := by
  sorry

/--
Within the class of locally graded groups, the $n$-Engel groups can be defined by identical
relations of the form $u = v$, where $u$ and $v$ are words without negative powers of variables:
for every $n \ge 1$ there is a set $S$ of positive laws such that a locally graded group $G$ is
$n$-Engel if and only if $G$ satisfies every law in $S$ (remark of O. Macedońska).

The editors' justification is that a locally graded $n$-Engel group is locally nilpotent
(Kim–Rhemtulla), hence an extension of a nilpotent group of $n$-bounded class by a group of
$n$-bounded exponent (Burns–Medvedev), and hence satisfies a positive law (Mal'cev).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.82».variants.locally_graded (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    ∃ S : Set (FreeMonoid ℕ × FreeMonoid ℕ),
      ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsLocallyGraded G →
        (IsNEngelGroup n G ↔ ∀ w ∈ S, SatisfiesPositiveLaw G w.1 w.2) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«2.82»

items: Commutator convention: the iterated Engel commutator is defined with [a,b] = a⁻¹b⁻¹ab (the convention of the Kourovka Notebook, Shirshov and Traustason), not Mathlib's ⁅a,b⁆ = a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹ used in Kourovka/1_40.lean. I verified by hand that the two conventions give the same class of n-Engel groups for n ≤ 3, but for fixed n ≥ 4 the equivalence is not obvious (e.g. the Mathlib-convention 4-Engel law is equivalent to the law [x,y,y][x,y,y,y]²[x,y,y,y,y] = [x,y,y,y][x,y,y][x,y,y,y] in the standard convention), so the notebook's convention is spelled out to guarantee the class of groups is exactly the notebook's. The API test engelCommutator_one records engelCommutator x y 1 = ⁅x⁻¹, y⁻¹⁆.

n ranges over ℕ with the hypothesis 0 < n (the statement's 'n-th Engel condition' with n copies of y); n = 0 would give the trivial variety, which is harmlessly positively definable, so the restriction does not change the mathematical content. The n ≤ 3 variant is stated with 0 < n ∧ n ≤ 3.

Positive words are elements of FreeMonoid ℕ (countably many variables x₀, x₁, …); the empty word (1) is allowed, so laws like xⁿ = 1 count as positive laws. Countably many variables suffice since every law involves finitely many variables.
The set S of positive laws may be infinite (the statement says 'identical relations', with no finiteness requirement); S is chosen depending only on n, before the group G.
Groups are quantified over Type (universe 0), as in the other Kourovka files; since laws are inherited by subgroups and invariant under isomorphism, this does not change the content.

IsLocallyGraded G := ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → H ≠ ⊥ → ∃ K : Subgroup H, K ≠ ⊤ ∧ K.FiniteIndex, i.e. every non-trivial finitely generated subgroup has a proper subgroup of finite index (equivalent to having a non-trivial finite quotient).

For the locally graded slot the biconditional is restricted to locally graded groups (S may depend on n only), following the table; the weaker reading ('such groups satisfy a positive law') is only described in the docstring.

Three small provable API theorems (category API) test the bespoke definitions: engelCommutator_one, isNEngelGroup_one_iff (1-Engel = abelian) and satisfiesPositiveLaw_of_mul_of_iff (the law x₀x₁ = x₁x₀ holds iff G is abelian).

reviewer_notes:
Final file = c01 with small docstring edits (module docstring now records the commutator convention; engelCommutator docstring rewrapped). Compiles with only 'declaration uses sorry' warnings; all lines ≤ 100 chars.

Deviation from the decomposition note: the note suggested reusing the Mathlib-convention engelCommutator of Kourovka/1_40.lean. I deliberately did not, because for fixed n the Mathlib convention ⁅a,b⁆ = aba⁻¹b⁻¹ is not known to define the same class of n-Engel groups as the notebook's [a,b] = a⁻¹b⁻¹ab (equivalent for n ≤ 3 by hand; for n = 4 the Mathlib-convention law reduces inside 4-Engel groups to [[x,y,y],[x,y,y,y]] = 1, i.e. to v b² [b,y] = b v b with v=[x,y,y], b=[x,y,y,y], as c01 also found independently). The candidates c04/c07 that asserted equivalence gave invalid arguments (the conjugating element depends on the iterate). Shirshov, Traustason, Kim–Rhemtulla and Burns–Medvedev all use a⁻¹b⁻¹ab, so the final file spells that convention out explicitly.

n = 0 is excluded (0 < n) in the main statement and the locally graded variant, following the table's 'intended n ≥ 1'; including it would not change truth values (0-Engel = trivial groups, defined by x₀ = x₁).

Locally graded slot: the editors' sketch literally only yields that locally graded n-Engel groups satisfy a positive law; the definability biconditional follows from it together with the standard fact that a variety satisfying a non-trivial positive law is defined by its positive laws (relatively free groups are groups of right fractions of their positive subsemigroups, and P_V is relatively free as a semigroup). The ⇐ direction then holds for all groups, so restricting to locally graded groups is harmless and matches the text.

Bespoke definitions (engelCommutator, IsNEngelGroup, SatisfiesPositiveLaw, IsLocallyGraded) are file-local with three proved @[category API] lemmas testing them (engelCommutator x y 1 = ⁅x⁻¹,y⁻¹⁆; 1-Engel ↔ abelian; the law x₀x₁ = x₁x₀ ↔ abelian). Also sanity-checked in a scratch file that IsNEngelGroup 0 G ↔ Subsingleton G and that engelCommutator x y 2 unfolds to the notebook's [[x,y],y].
statement:
Can the class of groups with the $n $th Engel condition $[x,\underbrace{y,\ldots ,y}_{n}]=1$ be defined by identical relations of the form $u=v$, where $u$ and $v$ are words without negative powers of variables? This can be done for $n=1,\,2,\,3$ (A. I. Shirshov, Algebra i Logika, 2, no. 5 (1963), 5–18 (Russian)).

Editors' comment: This has also been done for $n=4$ (G. Traustason, J. Group Theory, 2, no. 1 (1999), 39–46). As remarked by O. Macedońska, this is also true for the class of locally graded $n$-Engel groups because by (Y. Kim, A. Rhemtulla, in Groups–Korea'94, de Gruyter, Berlin, 1995, 189–197) such a group is locally nilpotent and then by (R. G. Burns, Yu. Medvedev, J. Austral. Math. Soc., 64 (1998), 92–100) such a group is an extension of a nilpotent group of $n$-bounded class by a group of $n$-bounded exponent; then a classical result of Mal'cev implies that such groups satisfy a positive law.
